llm.reply:
Marfan syndrome is a multisystem connective tissue disease with autosomal dominant inheritance, largely driven by FBN1 mutation [22: "Marfan syndrome (MFS) is a multisystem connective tissue disease with autosomal dominant inheritance"]. Its phenotype spans cardiovascular, ocular and skeletal findings, and presentation varies between patients [22: "often has different clinical manifestations"].

## MedGen Clinical Features

MedGen lists these clinical features: Aortic regurgitation [7], Arachnodactyly [11], Astigmatism [15], Ectopia lentis [19], Esotropia [23], Exotropia [25], Pes planus [26], Glaucoma [27], Congestive heart failure [28], Hypertropia [29] and Micrognathia [30].

## Diagnosis and Severity

Clinicians use the Ghent II nosology to diagnose the condition and to identify high-risk patients [24: "The Ghent II Nosology of MFS criteria are crucial in MFS diagnosis, guiding clinicians in identifying high-risk patients"]. The neonatal form is rare, severe and has a poor prognosis [22: "Neonatal MFS is especially rare with severe conditions and a poor prognosis"].

## Cardiovascular Focus in Trials

There is no curative treatment, but early diagnosis and treatment can extend survival [22: "there is still no radical treatment method for MFS, but early identification, early diagnosis, and early treatment can effectively prolong the life span of patients"]. Clinical trials target aortic root enlargement [8: "Slowing Aortic Root Enlargement in Individuals With Marfan Syndrome"]. One of these trials compares losartan with atenolol [16: "Losartan Versus Atenolol for the Treatment of Marfan Syndrome"].

MedGen lists these clinical features: Aortic regurgitation [7], Arachnodactyly [11], Astigmatism [15], Ectopia lentis [19], Esotropia [23], Exotropia [25], Pes planus [26], Glaucoma [27], Congestive heart failure [28], Hypertropia [29] and Micrognathia [30]. The MedGen record is titled Marfan syndrome [2]. The literature entity name is Marfan Syndrome [3].

## Genetic and Clinical Basis

Marfan syndrome is a dominantly inherited multisystem connective tissue disorder [22: "a multisystem connective tissue disease with autosomal dominant inheritance"]. It mostly results from FBN1 mutations [22: "It is mainly caused by FBN1 gene mutation"]. There is no curative therapy, but early diagnosis and treatment can extend survival [22: "early identification, early diagnosis, and early treatment can effectively prolong the life span of patients"]. The Ghent II criteria are central to diagnosis [24: "The Ghent II Nosology of MFS criteria are crucial in MFS diagnosis"].
